claim.why_it_matters: A reader of the markdown can apply the period-as-grouping-separator rule to the locale format of PICTURE, but the PDF limits it to the basic format (item b), so the transcription widens a normative editing rule.
claim.pdf_says: b) For the basic format of the PICTURE clause, the character written in character-strings, and inserted in numeric-edited items to represent the decimal separator shall be the comma. [indented under b):] NOTE 1 For the locale format of the PICTURE clause, ... [indented under b):] The character written in character-strings, and inserted in numeric-edited items to represent the grouping separator shall be the period. [back at rule 14's level:] The DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause has no effect on the editing or de-editing of a data item described with the locale format of the PICTURE clause.
claim.markdown_says:
b) For the basic format of the PICTURE clause, ... shall be the comma.

   NOTE 1 For the locale format of the PICTURE clause, ...

   The character written in character-strings, and inserted in numeric-edited items to represent the grouping separator shall be the period.

   The DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause has no effect on the editing or de-editing of a data item described with the locale format of the PICTURE clause.
claim.explanation: In the PDF, NOTE 1 and the grouping-separator sentence are indented as continuation paragraphs of item b) (the basic-format case), while the 'has no effect' sentence is at rule 14's own level. The markdown puts all three at the same indentation as a) and b) and as the rule-14-level sentence, so the grouping-separator rule is detached from b) and reads as applying to rule 14 generally, including the locale format of PICTURE, which the next sentence says DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA does not affect.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (ISO/IEC 1989:2002 p.203, PDF page 225) does show NOTE 1 and the grouping-separator sentence indented under b), with 'The DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause has no effect ... locale format of the PICTURE clause' at rule 14's body level, and the markdown flattens all of a), b), NOTE 1, the grouping sentence and the 'no effect' sentence to one 3-space indentation. The claim quotes both sources accurately. But every word is present and in the same order, and the difference is indentation only. It does not change the normative meaning: the very next sentence, present in the markdown immediately after the grouping-separator sentence, states that DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA has no effect on editing or de-editing of an item with the locale format of PICTURE. So a markdown reader cannot validly apply the period-as-grouping-separator exchange to the locale format; the scope the claim says is lost is restated explicitly. This is layout flattening, not a content discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Formatting only: the markdown flattens the nesting of rule 14's sub-paragraphs (NOTE 1 and the grouping-separator sentence printed as continuations of b)), but the text is complete and the following 'no effect on ... locale format' sentence keeps the locale-format scope unchanged.
